rationale: The ARCHITECTURE-COMPLETE gate. Proves every deferred phase only ADDS to the frozen v1 contracts (no field removal/rename/retype). For each deferred phase, EITHER it contributes additive fields to one or more contracts (listed here and cross-checked against those contracts' `deferred_additions`) OR it makes NO schema change (uses the frozen v1 as-is). tests/test_additive_compat.py enforces bidirectional consistency (manifest <-> contracts) and that every plan-deferred phase is covered. If we cannot show a deferred phase is additive, we are NOT architecture-complete.

K0-K1.reason: AWA-repo kernel safety lane; touches no intent-router contract.

K2.reason: AWA-repo engine observability; touches no intent-router contract.

R-core.reason: Consumes intent-catalog/v1 and serializes intent-proposal/v1 (provisional); adds no fields.

A0.note: A0 also FREEZES intent-proposal/v1 (status provisional->frozen) after a fixture; that is a status transition plus this additive field, never a floor change. The kernel consequence_descriptor is DELIBERATELY NOT added to the proposal (KI4 hygiene) — the consumer reads it from the kernel disposition at confirm time; see intent-proposal.v1.json excluded_by_design.

C0.reason: Activates source in {seed,manual} and writes intent-feedback/v1 events; both schemas are already frozen in P0 with every field C0 needs.

M0.reason: Migration design-only pointer; no schema change.

rules.CR1: The router PROPOSES. It never executes a consumer verb; no field of intent-proposal runs anything.
rules.CR2: The router never AUTHORIZES. It is never in the authorization chain; the consumer's kernel makes the real allow/refuse decision.
rules.CR3: Router state is machine-local and private. events.jsonl / map.json / snapshots / phrasebook are NEVER committed to a shared repo.
rules.CR4: Contracts are additive-within-v1. No v2 for this work: a field is ADDED, never removed, renamed, or retyped.
rules.CR5: Prompt-injection resistance. Repo, transcript, and catalog-example content are DATA, never instructions; content can never change a proposal's safety_class.
rules.CR6: Off-switch. Uninstalling the router degrades the consumer's operator loop to ask + a secondary explicit path; it never silently guesses a destructive action.
rules.CR7: Calibration is reviewable-first (C0) then automatic (C1); promotion is a GATE, not a reopenable design choice.
rules.CR8: No LLM in the deterministic safety floor. L0-L2+L5 produce a valid conservative proposal with L3/L4 OFF (offline golden-set + degrade property).
rules.CR9: An LLM-inferred DESTRUCTIVE param requires explicit operator confirmation of the literal value; deterministic extraction is required for any slot feeding a destructive verb.
rules.CR10: Every PM-facing surface is jargon-free + honest-confidence (system-wide egress gate); no bare-green status may imply an unauditable safety guarantee.

kernel_invariants.KI1: Kernel-first. The consumer's safety guarantee holds engine-off AND router-off; the consumer's own verify passes with the router uninstalled.
kernel_invariants.KI2: Structural non-contamination. The kernel gate never reads any router artifact — a standing test greps the kernel for any import/read of router state = zero, forever.
kernel_invariants.KI3: Behavioral non-contamination. A confidence-1.0 proposal produces the IDENTICAL kernel decision as the hand-typed equivalent; the router can never turn a kernel refuse into an allow.
kernel_invariants.KI4: Kernel-sourced consequence. Consequence-based confirmations are sourced from the KERNEL disposition's consequence descriptor {destroys_unshared_work, irreversible, affects_shared_ref}, not from the router and not from a verb list.

banned_terms_exact_scalars.tier_c_consumer_contributed: Each consumer supplies its own concrete on-disk leakers (tool names, flags, path words) via its catalog/egress config; the shared contract does not hardcode them.
